summary.zh: 醋饭与刺身的黄金比例，在家复刻江户前握寿司的手艺。
summary.en: The golden ratio of seasoned rice to sashimi — recreate Edomae nigiri craft at home.

steps.zh: 寿司米淘洗至水清澈，浸泡 30 分钟后按 1:1.1 的水米比煮熟。
steps.en: Rinse rice until the water runs clear, soak 30 minutes, then cook with a 1:1.1 water-to-rice ratio.

steps.zh: 米醋、糖、盐小火加热溶化，制成寿司醋，趁热拌入米饭，用切拌手法扇凉至体温。
steps.en: Warm vinegar, sugar and salt into sushi-zu; fold into hot rice with a cutting motion while fanning to body temperature.

steps.zh: 三文鱼逆纹切成 5 毫米厚、一口大小的薄片。
steps.en: Slice salmon against the grain into 5mm bite-sized pieces.

steps.zh: 手沾醋水，取 20 克醋饭轻握成椭圆形饭团，力度以内部空气感为准。
steps.en: With vinegar-wet hands, shape 20g rice into an oval — gentle pressure, keeping air inside.

steps.zh: 鱼片一面抹少许山葵，盖在饭团上，用指腹轻压贴合。
steps.en: Dab wasabi on the fish, lay it over the rice, and press lightly with fingertips to bond.

steps.zh: 摆盘，配寿司酱油与腌姜片，鱼的一面蘸酱油食用。
steps.en: Plate with soy sauce and gari; dip fish-side down when eating.

tips.zh: 醋饭温度保持在体温左右，鱼片才不会被烫熟。
tips.en: Keep rice at body temperature so it doesn't cook the fish.

tips.zh: 握饭要「外紧内松」，入口即散又不易掉粒。
tips.en: Shape rice firm outside, airy inside — it should fall apart in the mouth, not on the plate.

tips.zh: 切鱼一刀到底，不要来回锯，断面才光滑。
tips.en: Slice fish in one stroke — sawing tears the flesh.

failChecks.zh: 饭团散开：米饭太干或握得太松，检查水米比并稍加力度。
failChecks.en: Rice falling apart? Too dry or shaped too loosely — check water ratio and press slightly firmer.

failChecks.zh: 米饭太黏太酸：寿司醋过量或米饭过湿，按比例减醋。
failChecks.en: Mushy or sour rice? Too much sushi-zu or wet rice — reduce vinegar to ratio.

failChecks.zh: 有腥味：鱼不新鲜，务必选用刺身级并低温保存。
failChecks.en: Fishy smell? The fish isn't fresh — always use sashimi-grade, kept cold.

culturalStory.zh: 握寿司诞生于 19 世纪初的江户（今东京），华屋与兵卫在街头现握现卖，被称为「江户前寿司」，是当时日本人的快餐。三文鱼握寿司其实是挪威人的发明：1980 年代挪威三文鱼过剩，「日本计划」用了十余年才说服日本人接受生吃三文鱼，如今它已是在全球最受欢迎的握寿司。
culturalStory.en: Nigiri sushi was born in early 19th-century Edo (Tokyo), where Hanaya Yohei sold hand-pressed sushi as street fast food — the 'Edomae' style. Salmon nigiri is actually a Norwegian invention: in the 1980s, 'Project Japan' spent a decade persuading the Japanese to eat raw salmon. Today it is the world's most popular nigiri.
